literal: Affection unceasing kin if-joins, budding unceasing prosperity many will-give.
translation: If one secures kin whose affection never ceases, it will yield many forms of ever-budding prosperity.
modern: அன்பு குறையாத சுற்றத்தார் ஒருவருக்கு அமைந்தால், அது அவருக்குத் தொடர்ந்து வளரும் பல செல்வங்களைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the value of maintaining close ties with loving relatives. The phrase 'viruppu aṟā' describes kin whose affection is never severed. When a person is surrounded by such people, it brings 'aruppu aṟā ākkam', meaning prosperity that never stops budding or growing. The imagery of a continuously budding plant illustrates how supportive relationships naturally and endlessly generate success and wealth.
